'When this leaves the arena, banish the top card of YOUR deck. If it's a non-attack action card, you may play it this turn as though it were an instant.'

The payoff was BANISH_OPP_TOP_GRANT_PLAY, which is Infiltrate's effect: it banishes the top card of the OPPONENT's deck. So the card banished twice -- once from each deck -- and the permission it granted was for a card that has nothing to do with the one its own text is about. Its 'target': 'top_deck' was unread, because that effect takes no target.

The condition was wrong in a second, quieter way: it asked CARD_IN_ZONE about the top of the deck AFTER the banish had already moved that card, so it was inspecting whatever card came next. 'If IT is a non-attack action card' is about the card just banished, which is what the `banished` ref holds -- and 'non-attack action' is two claims (it IS an Action, it is NOT an Attack), so it is two REF_IS_TYPE checks and not one.

The start-of-turn destroy is gated on IS_ACTIVE_PLAYER: 'at the beginning of YOUR action phase' fires on the controller's turn, not on both.

APPROXIMATED: 'as though it were an instant' is a one-shot grant matched by card PROPERTIES, and the queue cannot name one object, so the grant matches the first non-attack Action card played rather than specifically the banished one. The play PERMISSION is identity-based (GRANT_PLAY_FROM_BANISHED acts on the ref), so the card that may be played is exactly right; only the timing grant is broader. Definition of done: an object_ref on GRANT_INSTANT_TIMING, as MODIFY_NEXT_ATTACK already has.
